result.title: Tokens as Locality-Preserving Anchors: Scalable Novel View Synthesis with Target-Adaptive Token Routing
result.summary: Transformer-based view synthesis models render each target viewpoint from the source images, without an explicit 3D representation, which lets them reproduce fine detail and view-dependent effects. However, their decoder attends to every source token for every frame, so rendering slows with each source image. Rasterization avoids this by culling primitives that the viewpoint does not see, but source tokens cannot be culled this way, as they have no explicit position or extent. Our key insight is that source tokens are nonetheless spatial anchors: each encodes a local region of the scene, so the decoder's attention for any viewpoint concentrates on a few of them. A lightweight router predicts these tokens from the source tokens and the viewpoint, and the decoder attends only to a fixed budget of top-ranked tokens, so its cost no longer depends on the number of source tokens. We supervise the router with the decoder's attention, using non-maximum suppression to demote redundant tokens. With 24 source images and two views' worth of tokens, our model renders 6.4 times faster than LagerNVS, at a PSNR only 0.68 dB lower. One ranking serves every budget, so the budget can change at render time.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把源图像 token 视为保持局部性的空间锚点，用轻量路由器依据源 token 与视点预测少量关键 token，使解码器只在固定预算的 top-ranked token 上做注意力，渲染成本不再随源图数量增长；路由器以解码器注意力为监督，并用非极大值抑制压低冗余 token。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用注意力监督学习 token 排序、固定预算筛选与冗余抑制」可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选和随预算伸缩的 latent 计算分配提供线索，但论文面向新视角合成，与多模态推理无直接关系，迁移价值需核查。
